<!-- version: 2.41.1 -->
If you back your database up to a WebDAV server, this release is worth installing promptly. On some servers - a Synology NAS is the common case - the clean-up that keeps only the last few backups was working from the wrong end: every run uploaded a fresh backup and deleted it again moments later, while the oldest ones stayed. A household could have had the feature switched on for months and never actually held a recent backup off-site. That is fixed, and the clean-up will no longer delete a backup it has just uploaded, whatever else goes wrong. Your existing remote folder keeps the older backups it held on to; the next scheduled run starts adding current ones alongside them. Nothing needs configuring.

Calendar events also stopped changing colour on their own. Opening an event and changing anything - even just the title - could repaint it in a different colour, because the colour picker did not recognise colours from outside its own palette and quietly replaced them on save. That affected events coloured after the person they were assigned to, and events that brought their own colour in from a synced calendar. The picker now shows whatever colour an event actually has, and saving without touching the colour leaves it alone. It also no longer greys itself out when someone is assigned to the event, so you can set any event's colour deliberately. Events that were already recoloured keep the colour they were given - set them once more and it will stay.

Full release notes are available at https://github.com/ulsklyc/yuvomi/releases/tag/v2.41.1
